title: Si Bien: Granting a Point About Music

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *si bien* from B2 Unit 8: a formal way to say "although it is true that", with the indicative. The speaker grants a true point and then says what matters more. Music history is full of such points: a style was born in one place and became famous in another, or it was criticised and then loved.

sections.title: Grant the point, then say the main idea
rows: Si bien la salsa no nació en la isla, muchos puertorriqueños fueron figuras importantes.
grants a true point (born elsewhere), then the main idea
Si bien el reggaetón fue criticado, hoy se escucha en todo el mundo.
grants the criticism, then the main idea
La bomba, si bien nació en las plantaciones, hoy se baila en festivales.
*si bien* in the middle, between commas

items.spanish: Si bien la bomba nació en las plantaciones, hoy se baila en festivales de toda la isla.
items.english: Although bomba was born on the plantations, today it is danced at festivals all over the island.

items.spanish: Si bien la plena nació en Ponce, hoy se toca en toda la isla.
items.english: Although plena was born in Ponce, today it is played all over the island.

items.spanish: Si bien la salsa se formó en Nueva York, muchos de sus músicos eran de origen puertorriqueño.
items.english: Although salsa took shape in New York, many of its musicians were of Puerto Rican origin.

items.spanish: El reggaetón, si bien tiene influencias de Panamá y Jamaica, nació en San Juan.
items.english: Reggaeton, although it has influences from Panama and Jamaica, was born in San Juan.

sections.content: *Si bien* is formal and takes the indicative, because the fact is true. Do not add *que* after it, and do not use the subjunctive: for "even if" you need *aunque*. In a message to a friend, *aunque* is more natural; *si bien* fits an article or a talk.
